narrativeBlocks.title: A feast interrupted by mist
narrativeBlocks.body: Manawydan — Bran's brother and Branwen's widower-friend — is feasting with Rhiannon and her son Pryderi when a white mist rolls in. When it clears, the palace and every person in it has vanished.

narrativeBlocks.title: An empty kingdom
narrativeBlocks.body: The three survivors — Manawydan, Rhiannon, Pryderi — walk a depopulated landscape. Pryderi follows a strange boar into a fort and doesn't come out; Rhiannon follows and vanishes too.

narrativeBlocks.title: Alone and patient
narrativeBlocks.body: Manawydan alone stays — not fighting, not raging, just present. He plants wheat, harvests it, lives quietly in the ruined land, because the other way is already tried.

narrativeBlocks.title: The mouse's secret
narrativeBlocks.body: When a mouse steals his grain, he catches it — and instead of killing it, ties it up to hang. A stranger arrives offering ransom for it: the 'mouse' is the enchanter's wife, and the spell is broken for her life.

narrativeBlocks.title: Patience as victory
narrativeBlocks.body: Where Greek heroes win by doing, Manawydan wins by waiting and noticing — the Welsh hero-ideal is different: quiet attention, not force, breaks the enchantment.

quiz.prompt: What happens when the mist clears?

choices.text: The castle is buried in snow
The palace and all its people have vanished — only Manawydan, Rhiannon, and Pryderi remain in an empty land

quiz.explanation: The mist takes the whole population — the enchantment is total.

quiz.prompt: How is the enchantment finally broken?

choices.text: Manawydan catches the enchanter's wife disguised as a mouse and ransoms her for the people's return

quiz.explanation: Patience plus a single caught mouse — the Welsh hero wins by waiting.
